big_idea: We use length, mass, and capacity to compare and measure. We pick the right way for each job.
learning_intention: We are learning to compare and measure things in three ways.
student_learning_goal: I can compare and measure things in different ways.
success_criteria: I can compare lengths by lining up.
I can compare mass on a balance.
I can compare capacity by pouring.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Max and Tess — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.
All length / mass / capacity manipulatives at 3 carnival stations
Lesson 5 capstone rubric — provided in assessment_suite stage

minds_on.activity_name: Max and Tess at the Carnival
minds_on.hook: Max: Welcome to the MEASUREMENT CARNIVAL! Three stations: LENGTH, MASS, CAPACITY. Pick your favourite!
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Max + Tess in carnival hats. 'CAPSTONE day! We use everything: LENGTH, MASS, CAPACITY, MEASURING.'

Lightning review: 'Length — LINE UP. Mass — BALANCE. Capacity — POUR. Cubes — TOUCHING, count.'

The carnival: 3 stations + carnival template.
- A: LENGTH — order 5 ribbons; measure favourite with cubes
- B: MASS — balance 5 objects, find heaviest + find a same-weight pair
- C: CAPACITY — pour 4 cups, find biggest + find a same-capacity pair

Each child rotates all 3, records on their CARNIVAL TEMPLATE.

'Max says — pick the RIGHT tool. Length tool, mass tool, capacity tool.'

Max's RULE: 'LINE IT UP — COMPARE — NAME IT!' Today: line up the right tool, compare, name the result.

Class refrain. Class chants 3x with claps: 'LINE IT UP — COMPARE — NAME IT! That's how Max measures!'

'Today YOU are the measurement experts!'
student_actions: Watch Max and Tess introduce the carnival.
Plan which station to start at.

steps.instruction: Hand out carnival templates. Each child rotates through 3 stations (~7 min each).
steps.teacher_prompt: Say: 'Three stations. Record on your template. Pick your favourites!'

steps.instruction: Station A (LENGTH): Order 5 ribbons from shortest to longest. Pick favourite. Measure with cubes.
Station B (MASS): Use balance to find heaviest of 5 objects. Find a same-weight pair.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say: 'Balance to find heavy. Find same.'

steps.instruction: Station C (CAPACITY): Pour to find which holds most of 4 cups. Find a same-capacity pair.
Circulate to record summative evidence on the capstone rubric.
steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each child. Ask 'Show me.' Mark the rubric.

differentiation.for_emerging: Spend more time at Station A only. Skip stretch.
differentiation.for_extending: After all 3 stations: pick a 4th measurement question and answer it independently — e.g., 'is my desk longer than my partner's hand-spans by HOW MANY?'.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Provide picture-cued sentence frames on the template. 'I found ___ holds most.'
differentiation.for_movement_learners: NO-PAPER, NO-PURCHASE PATH: replace each station tool with bodies. Length: stand-against-the-wall back-to-back comparisons. Mass: human-balance arms-out two-object compare. Capacity: pour beans between any classroom cups (no carnival template — sticky-note results). Whole capstone can run with bodies + everyday classroom objects only.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Four signals: completes length comparison; uses balance correctly; pours for capacity; measures with cubes.

discussion_prompts: Which station was your favourite — and why?
How do you compare length? (LINE IT UP at one end.)
How do you compare mass? (BALANCE — heavier side drops.)
How do you compare capacity? (POUR — overflow means LESS.)
Which way is best for measuring a desk? (Hand-spans for medium, cubes for short, footsteps for long.)
consolidation.exit_routine: Refrain chant 3x. Then each child shows their template and finishes the sentence frame: 'My favourite measurement was ___ because ___.' Sticky-note one capstone finding and post.

assessment_in_this_lesson.evidence_collected: Capstone template with results from all 3 stations.
assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 5 captures A10.1 and A10.2 mastery in one integrated capstone.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child uses one measurement type for everything — repairing the attribute-tool mismatch at K capstone (Sarama & Clements, 2009; Lehrer, 2003)
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On the K measurement capstone, the most-documented integrative trap is the attribute-tool mismatch: child has practiced four moves (line up, balance, pour, count cubes) but doesn't yet attend to which ATTRIBUTE the question is asking about — so they pick whichever tool is closest to hand and apply it indiscriminately (cubes for everything, or balance for everything).

Lehrer (2003) describes this as the pre-measurement 'tool-bound' phase: the move (counting cubes) is fluent but is not yet driven by a question about an attribute. Sarama & Clements (2009) synthesise the K-G2 measurement trajectory: the integrative end-of-K target is to articulate the question first ('how LONG / how HEAVY / how MUCH it HOLDS?'), and let the question pick the tool. The capstone is where this naming step gets exercised.

Why this matters: without the attribute-first move, children reach Grade 1 still treating measurement as 'whatever-tool-the-teacher-handed-me' rather than 'the right tool for the question'. The capstone is the first time they're asked to choose unaided.

The walkthrough covers when a child uses the wrong tool because they haven't named the attribute.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Capstone session. Child is at Station C (capacity). Trying to put cubes inside a cup to compare. Says 'how many cubes does this cup hold?'.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'You're MEASURING the cup with cubes! That's clever. But what is the QUESTION about? Length, mass, or capacity?'

The child names CAPACITY. 'Right — and capacity, we POUR. Cubes work for LENGTH.'

Walk through. 'Max says — NAME the attribute, then pick the tool. Length → LINE UP. Mass → BALANCE. Capacity → POUR.'

Generalise. 'Cubes are GREAT — for length. For capacity, BEANS or WATER fill the shape.'

Now practice. Pour beans into both cups. Compare overflow. 'Pouring tells us which holds more.'

If still using cubes for capacity: take cubes away; hand the child beans + two cups. 'Use these.' Force the right-tool behaviour, but keep tying it back to NAMING the attribute first.

Long-term recovery: every capstone task starts with the child naming the attribute aloud, then choosing the tool.
expected_student_responses: (Confused) Uses cubes / balance for everything; doesn't name the attribute first.
(Mid) Picks right tool with the 'what's the question?' prompt.
(Strong) Names the attribute aloud, then picks the matching tool, for all 3 stations.
(Stretched) Uses 2 tools to verify (cubes AND hand-spans for length); explains why the result matches across tools.
common_misconceptions: Cubes measure everything. (Repair: cubes are for length only — for capacity, pour; for mass, balance.)
Balance compares length. (Repair: balance is for mass — gravity pulls heavier down.)
All measurement looks the same. (Repair: 3 attributes, 3 different tools — the QUESTION picks the tool.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child uses cubes for capacity (or balance for length): pause and ask 'what is the QUESTION? Length, mass, or capacity?'; only after the child names the attribute, hand them the matching tool; do this for the next 3 station-rotations until naming becomes automatic.

DIAGNOSTIC B — child grabs a tool before reading the station card: cover the tools with a cloth; require the child to read or hear the station question, name the attribute, AND tell you which tool is needed BEFORE the cloth is removed; tools stay covered until the attribute is named.

DIAGNOSTIC C — child names the attribute correctly but picks the wrong tool from the carnival pile: post the 3-attribute / 3-tool chart at eye level (LENGTH—LINE UP, MASS—BALANCE, CAPACITY—POUR); make the child point to their station's row before reaching for a tool.

worksheet_brief.purpose: Summative artifact applying A10.1 and A10.2.

parts_outline.task: Length: Order 4 strips from shortest to longest. Measure favourite in cubes.
Mass: Mark which side of the balance goes down for 3 pairs.
Capacity: Circle the cup that holds more in 3 pairs. Find a same-capacity pair.
